questions.question: According to a recent Supreme Court ruling, the 24-hour period for producing a detained person before a Magistrate begins from which point?
options: The filing of the FIR against the individual
The actual detention of the individual
The moment the individual is charged
The formal arrest of the individual
questions.explanation: The Supreme Court recently ruled that the 24-hour period for producing a detained person before a Magistrate, as stipulated by fundamental rights, begins from the actual detention of the individual, not from the point of formal arrest. The Court emphasized that fundamental rights supersede even special laws like UAPA and PMLA.
questions.background: Article 22(2) of the Indian Constitution mandates that every person arrested and detained in custody shall be produced before the nearest Magistrate within a period of 24 hours of such arrest, excluding the time necessary for the journey from the place of arrest to the Magistrate's court. This ruling clarifies the commencement of this crucial period.
questions.examRelevance: SC clarified that the 24-hour period for production before a Magistrate starts from detention, not formal arrest.

source.title: 24-hour to produce before Magistrate starts from detention, not ‘formal arrest’: Supreme Court
